answer: An agent economy can anchor each identity to one tidal lagoon gate that only its holder may operate. The gate's lock turns on a cipher dial set by that week's tide tables, so the holder must be physically present to open it on schedule, and a licensed harbor warden inspects each gate in person, one per day, with no bulk licences. A forge in the harbor town stamps each gate's unique iron key, one per identity, never twice. Each extra fake costs another lagoon lease, another forged key, another human at the gate, and a license fee in outside money doubling per gate on the same funding trail.
